title: 20 Classic Turkish Mezes Explained: What to Order at a Meyhane
seoTitle: 20 Classic Turkish Mezes: What to Order at a Meyhane
metaDescription: Turkish meze guide covering 20 cold and hot meyhane dishes, how the Istanbul meze tray works, and how many plates two people should order.
quickAnswer: A traditional Turkish meyhane meal begins with cold mezes—cured fish like lakerda, strained yoghurt dips such as haydari and atom, and olive-oil vegetables like fava and şakşuka—followed by hot starters (ara sıcak) before any main course arrives. Two diners typically share four to six cold plates plus two hot dishes over a long, unhurried evening.

body.text: Understanding a turkish meze guide changes how you dine across Istanbul and the Turkish coast. In a proper meyhane, food is paced for conversation rather than rushed courses, a rhythm highlighted in [GoTürkiye's Istanbul Meyhane Culture guide](https://goturkiye.com/istanbul/meyhane-culture). Below are 20 classic dishes—split between cold openings and warm mid-meal plates—plus the practical ordering etiquette locals rely on.
What are the essential cold mezes (lakerda, atom, haydari, fava, köpoğlu, muhammara, şakşuka)?

Cold mezes (soğuk mezeler) anchor every meyhane table and arrive immediately after drinks are poured. Essential plates balance brine, acidity, olive oil, and dairy: cured bonito (lakerda), chilli-butter yoghurt (atom), herbed strained yoghurt (haydari), broad-bean purée (fava), fried vegetables under yoghurt (köpoğlu), spiced walnut-pepper paste (muhammara), and tomato-braised aubergine (şakşuka).

Rounding out the 15 classic cold plates you will spot across Istanbul—from Beyoğlu backstreets to Kadıköy fish markets—are ezine peyniri with kavun (aged white cheese and ripe melon), patlıcan salatası (smoky charred aubergine), deniz börülcesi (garlicky sea samphire), acılı ezme (finely chopped spicy tomato-pepper relish), humus (warm or cool chickpea-tahini purée), çiroz (dried, shredded mackerel with dill and olive oil), levrek marin (citrus-cured sea bass), and barbunya pilaki (borlotti beans braised in olive oil). As [GoTürkiye's Istanbul Gastronomy Capital overview](https://goturkiye.com/gastronomy/blog/istanbul-a-gastronomy-capital) notes, dry-salted bonito served with red onion and dill remains one of the city's benchmark seafood starters.

body.text: Which hot starters (paçanga böreği, kalamar, ahtapot, arnavut ciğeri) follow?

Hot starters, known as ara sıcak ("warm in-between"), arrive once the table has spent forty-five minutes to an hour picking through cold mezes. The five defining classics are crisp paçanga böreği (pastırma and kaşar cheese rolled in yufka), fried kalamar tava with walnut-garlic tarator, charcoal-grilled ahtapot ızgara (octopus), spiced arnavut ciğeri (pan-fried lamb liver), and bubbling karides güveç (butter-garlic clay-pot prawns).

These five warm dishes complete the core 20 mezes every first-time visitor should recognise. Order ara sıcak only when you are genuinely ready for warm food; kitchen staff time them to hit the table piping hot. Pair crispy fried calamari with lemon and tarator sauce, and ask for arnavut ciğeri with sumac-tossed red onions to cut through the richness. According to [GoTürkiye's Turkish Cuisine guide](https://goturkiye.com/gastronomy/turkish-cuisine), layering light olive-oil starters before richer hot plates keeps a multi-hour meal comfortable rather than heavy.
How does choosing from the meze tray work at a traditional Istanbul meyhane?

At a classic Istanbul meyhane, a waiter approaches your table carrying a wide aluminium tray—or invites you to a glass-fronted display cabinet—loaded with ten to twenty pre-plated cold mezes. You simply point to the dishes you want, ask what was prepared fresh that afternoon, and confirm whether seasonal cured fish such as lakerda or çiroz is available.
Tray service is visual by design, so you rarely need a printed menu for the first round. Still, a quick routine prevents misunderstandings and surprise charges:

items: Ask prices for seafood mezes: Cured lakerda, octopus salad, and marinated sea bass cost significantly more than yoghurt or vegetable dips.
Check the bread and cover charge: Many historic taverns charge a modest per-person kuver covering bread, butter, and water; verify it on the menu before ordering.
Inspect oil gloss and herbs: Freshly dressed olive-oil plates look bright rather than dried at the edges, and dill or parsley should be vivid green.
Start with white cheese and melon: Locals almost always open with a plate of aged white cheese and melon before touching heavier garlic dishes.

body.text: How many mezes should two people order?

Two people should order four to five cold mezes for the first hour, followed by one or two hot starters (ara sıcak). If you plan to skip a main course—which most Istanbul regulars do—five cold plates and two warm dishes provide a full, balanced dinner without leaving half-eaten bowls behind.

Over-ordering at minute one is the single most common mistake visitors make. Cold mezes are served in generous sharing portions, and warm bread disappears quickly alongside dips like haydari and muhammara. Start conservatively, pace your drinks, and add a second round of hot starters only if you still have room. faq.q: What is the difference between a meyhane and an ocakbaşı?
faq.a: A meyhane centres on cold mezes, seafood, and slow-paced conversation over rakı or wine, whereas an ocakbaşı focuses on charcoal-grilled kebabs cooked right in front of diners around a central copper hearth.

faq.q: Are Turkish cold mezes suitable for vegetarians and vegans?
faq.a: Most vegetable and legume mezes—including fava, şakşuka, deniz börülcesi, muhammara, and barbunya pilaki—are naturally vegan, while yoghurt-based dips such as haydari and atom suit vegetarians. Always confirm that fish roe or butter was not added.

faq.q: Do I have to drink rakı at a traditional meyhane?
faq.a: No. While anise-flavoured rakı is the classic pairing, reputable Istanbul meyhanes serve Turkish wines, beer, and non-alcoholic options like sparkling water, turnip juice (şalgam), and fresh lemonade without hesitation.

faq.q: Why is lakerda more expensive than other cold mezes?
faq.a: Authentic lakerda is made from large migratory bonito (torik) caught in late autumn, carefully cleaned, and salt-cured for weeks before resting in oil, making it a labour-intensive seasonal delicacy.

faq.q: Should you order a main course after mezes and hot starters?
faq.a: It is completely optional. Many local tables share five or six cold mezes and two hot starters as their entire meal, skipping grilled fish or meat mains altogether.

faq.q: How early should you book a popular Istanbul meyhane?
faq.a: For well-known taverns in Beyoğlu, Karaköy, Cihangir, or Kadıköy on Friday and Saturday nights, booking three to seven days ahead is advisable, especially for tables of four or more.
